To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The educational attainment of South African youth is strongly influenced by their family background.
1) the racial gap in educational achievement in South Africa has not changed in 15 years, and 2) the gap is not explained by family structure, family resources, or school characteristics.

(1) the educational advantage of Indian/Asian and white youth is greater in the post-apartheid era, (2) the disadvantage of Africans in educational attainment is greater in the 2000s compared to the 1990s, (3) the disadvantage of coloureds in educational attainment is smaller in the 2005s compared to the early 1990s and (4) family background is the most important determinant of educational attainment, and the school is the least important.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: the extent of racial inequality in educational outcomes; the extent to which racial inequality is due to differences in family structure, family background, school resources and school quality; and the extent to which family structure, family resources, school resources and quality mediate racial differences in educational attainment.
the role that family structure, resources, and school quality play in explaining the race differences in educational attainment.

the family institution, and the family structure and resources within it, is central to understanding educational inequalities in South Africa.
race differences in educational attainment in post-aparheid South Africa are largely because of family structure and resources.

racial inequality in educational attainment is largely a function of racial inequality in family structure and family resources.
